_meta.description: SR2 core's stock cyberdeck price list (p.173), adapted to plug directly into this app's existing VR2-flavored matrix engine (app/services/matrix_engine.py, app/routers/matrix_runs.py, frontend/deck-workshop.html). Decisions logged in docs/sr2-character-builder-plan.md.
_meta.source: docs/reference-data/shadowrun2e-com/gear-data.js (cat:"deck", src:"SR2", pg:173) -- SR2 core book stats, transcribed from the reference site.
_meta.not_included: SuzyQ's Cyberdeck (VR2 p.90) is NOT duplicated here -- it's already VR2-native (explicit persona ratings, ASIST, ICCM) and stays as-is in gear-data.js. This file is specifically the SR2-core stock decks adapted forward, not a combined catalog.

dropped_fields.load: SR2's printed 'Load' stat has no representation anywhere in app/ -- the engine already gates 'how much can you run' via Active Memory + per-program Mp cost (rating^2 x multiplier), which covers the same conceptual ground. Decision: drop Load entirely rather than build new plumbing for a redundant second capacity stat. Not included on any entry below.

persona_pool_rule.description: Stock SR2-core decks do NOT come with fixed Bod/Evasion/Masking/Sensor ratings -- that's true to the book (only custom VR2 builds like SuzyQ's specify them) and matches the app's existing DeckerStats schema, which already requires the buyer to populate all four individually.
persona_pool_rule.rule: At purchase (or whenever a deck changes hands), the buyer assigns Bod/Evasion/Masking/Sensor from a pool of MPCP x 3 points (SR2 p.174, personaCapMult in builder-data.js). If the deck has a Reality Filter installed, the cap uses (MPCP - 1) x 3 instead -- see app/routers/matrix_runs.py:6472-6476.
persona_pool_rule.field_below: persona_pool -- the total points available to split; not a fixed split.

io_speed_rule.description: SR2 core's printed I/O rating (a small 1-50 number) is a DIFFERENT SCALE from the app's io_speed field, which is Mp-per-Combat-Turn bandwidth (matches VR2's own convention -- SuzyQ's I/O Speed is 480, not a small rating). No book-sourced conversion exists between the two scales, so the printed I/O values are dropped and replaced with this derived rule instead of a guessed conversion factor.
io_speed_rule.app_max_validator: io_speed <= mpcp * sensor * 10 (app/routers/matrix_runs.py:6485) -- this is the hard ceiling the app already enforces.
io_speed_rule.house_rule_decided_2026-08-14: Off-the-shelf stock decks ship at HALF that ceiling, leaving headroom for upgrades: io_speed = mpcp * sensor * 5.
io_speed_rule.worked_example: MPCP 8 deck, buyer assigns Sensor 4 -> max = 8*4*10 = 320, stock I/O = 8*4*5 = 160.
io_speed_rule.rounding_rule_confirmed_2026-08-15: mpcp * sensor * 5 is only a multiple of 10 (the app's other io_speed requirement, matrix_runs.py:6485) when mpcp*sensor is even. When it's odd (e.g. MPCP 3 + Sensor 3 = 45), round UP to the nearest multiple of 10 (ceil(mpcp*sensor*5 / 10) * 10, i.e. add 5). Example: MPCP 3 + Sensor 3 -> raw 45 -> stock io_speed 50.
io_speed_rule.consequence: io_speed is therefore NOT a fixed stat on a stock deck -- it must be computed at persona-assignment time from whatever Sensor rating the buyer actually picks. No io_speed field is included per-deck below; compute it live using this rule.

_meta.known_app_inconsistency_unrelated_to_thi: docs/reference-data/shadowrun2e-com/builder-data.js cites the Active Memory cap as MPCP x 50 (SR2 p.172), but the live app validators (matrix_runs.py:6481, deck-workshop.html:2324) enforce MPCP x 100. Doesn't affect any deck below (all fit under both caps) -- logged so it isn't lost.
